points.description: States that the queue is stored in a circular array (also called a ring buffer or wrap-around array), so that when the rear pointer reaches the end of the array it wraps around to the start instead of shifting the queue.
points.partial_credit: Half credit for naming a circular array/ring buffer without saying the rear wraps around; no credit for a plain linear array that shifts elements.

levels.says: Mentions a circular array, ring buffer, or wrap-around array but does not say the rear pointer wraps around or otherwise convey reuse of the array slots.

points.description: States that the front of the queue is kept toward the beginning of the array and the rear toward the end, i.e. front and rear indices/pointers mark the occupied range.
points.partial_credit: Half credit for mentioning front and rear pointers or indices without stating their placement.

levels.says: Mentions front and rear pointers or indices but does not say that the front is toward the beginning and the rear toward the end.

rubric.notes: Full marks require the circular-array idea with the rear pointer wrapping around and the front/rear placement. A partly correct answer that names a circular array but omits wrap-around earns half of P1; naming front/rear pointers without placement earns half of P2. A plain linear array with shifting elements earns no marks for P1.
